Incorporating standard monetary policy literature, this FOMC statement is hawkish. With inflation well above target and unemployment low, the Committee’s 50 bp hike to 4.25–4.50% and guidance for “ongoing increases” align with Taylor-rule prescriptions that call for more-than-one-for-one responses to inflation to ensure a restrictive real policy rate. Emphasis on lags and cumulative tightening is consistent with Woodford’s expectations-centric view that credible commitments and clear guidance anchor inflation expectations, while avoiding oversteering given long and variable transmission. The plan to keep reducing Treasury and agency MBS holdings reinforces tightening via the credit and term-premia channels highlighted by Bernanke and coauthors, meaning financial conditions will tighten beyond the funds rate alone. Acknowledgment of Ukraine-related supply shocks fits the literature’s recommendation to prevent second-round effects rather than accommodate persistent inflation. The operational focus on the policy rate and corridor tools (ON RRP/RP) reflects Poole’s instrument-choice insights and the post-1980s shift away from money targeting toward interest rate control. Net tone: restrictive and credibility-focused, yet data-dependent.
